# Model and source

Liu et al. (2026) re-analysed individual patient data from four Pfizer trials of
sunitinib 50 mg once daily on the 4-weeks-on / 2-weeks-off (4/2) schedule in
metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), to ask whether the positive
exposure-efficacy relationship reported earlier survives time-dependent bias and
baseline confounding. Two models from the paper are shipped:

* `Liu_2026_sunitinib` -- the joint population PK model of sunitinib and its
  active metabolite SU12662 (294 patients, four trials; Supplementary Material S2,
  Table S2).
* `Liu_2026_sunitinib_multistate` -- the six-state multistate model of response,
  progression, discontinuation and death in the 165 cytokine-refractory patients of
  studies 1006 and 014 (Supplementary Material S3, Table S4).

The PK model supplies the exposure metric the paper tested in the multistate model,
AUCss,DOSE50,CLcycle1 (equation 1). Exposure was not retained in the final
multistate model: after adjustment for albumin and age it had no independent
effect on progression or survival (Table 2), so the two shipped models are not
linked.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2026_sunitinib"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70447>
* PMC record with Supplementary Materials S1-S3:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13468949/>

# Population

The PK analysis pooled 294 patients with sunitinib and SU12662 concentrations under
the 50 mg 4/2 regimen: 105 from study 1006 and 60 from study 014 (both
cytokine-refractory, phase II) and 42 from study 1034 and 88 from study 1065
(treatment-naive). The data held 1688 sunitinib and 1715 SU12662 total plasma
concentrations, mostly troughs in the on-treatment weeks and at the end of the
2-week break, for up to 5 cycles (Table 1; Supplementary S2).

The exposure-response set is the 165 cytokine-refractory patients of studies 1006
and 014 (Supplementary Table S1): mean age 57.1 years (SD 10.3, range 24-87), mean
weight 85.0 kg (SD 18.6), 35% women, 92% White, albumin 40.4 g/L (SD 4.8),
haemoglobin 124.3 g/L (SD 18.8), ECOG 0 in 55% and 1 in 44%, and a mean 38.0
months since diagnosis (SD 53.6). Dose reductions to 37.5 or 25 mg occurred in 38.2%.
The PK-model covariates are centred on the medians of the 294-patient PK dataset
(age 60 years, albumin 41 g/L, weight 82.4 kg), which the paper does not tabulate
further.

The same information is available programmatically through each model's
`population` metadata, e.g. `readModelDb("Liu_2026_sunitinib")()$population`.

# Population PK model

## Virtual cohort and simulation

Two hundred virtual patients are drawn from the exposure-response set demographics
of Supplementary Table S1 (normal distributions truncated at the observed ranges;
35% women). Each receives the first two 4/2 cycles of 50 mg once daily. The
sunitinib dose is entered in both `depot` (sunitinib) and `depot_su12662` (the
SU12662 input); the model's `f()` applies F and F * fm. Observations are made on
the ODE states with `dvid` set, because the model declares two endpoints.

```{r pk-cohort}
# Typical-value solves (omega zeroed) and the multistate model (no IIV in the
# source) solve several subjects without random effects, which rxode2 notes
# with a warning; that one message is expected here and is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Liu_2026_sunitinib")
n_pk <- 200
rtn <- function(n, m, s, lo, hi) {
  x <- rnorm(n, m, s)
  while (any(out <- x < lo | x > hi)) x[out] <- rnorm(sum(out), m, s)
  x
}
set.seed(2026)
cohort_pk <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_pk),
  AGE = rtn(n_pk, 57.1, 10.3, 24, 87),
  WT = rtn(n_pk, 85.0, 18.6, 45, 150),
  ALB = rtn(n_pk, 40.4, 4.8, 20, 49),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_pk, 1, 0.35)
)

dose_days <- c(0:27, 42:69)
dosing_pk <- expand.grid(id = cohort_pk$id, day = dose_days, cmt = c("depot", "depot_su12662"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  mutate(time = 24 * day, evid = 1L, amt = 50, dvid = NA_integer_) |>
  select(-day)
# Daily troughs for both cycles plus a rich profile over day 27 (the last
# on-treatment dosing interval of cycle 1).
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(24 * (0:84), 648 + c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 23.99))))
obs_pk <- expand.grid(id = cohort_pk$id, time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
events_pk <- bind_rows(dosing_pk, obs_pk) |>
  left_join(cohort_pk, by = "id") |>
  mutate(treatment = "50 mg QD 4/2") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261)
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = events_pk, keep = "treatment",
  returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(Ctot = Cc + Cc_su12662)
```

```{r pk-figure, fig.cap = "Simulated trough concentrations of sunitinib, SU12662 and their sum over the first two 4/2 cycles (median and 10th-90th percentiles, 200 virtual patients). Compare with the observed data in Supplementary Figure S2 and the VPC in Supplementary Figure S4 of Liu 2026."}
sim_pk |>
  filter(time %% 24 == 0, time >= 24) |>
  select(id, time, Sunitinib = Cc, SU12662 = Cc_su12662, Total = Ctot) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Sunitinib, SU12662, Total), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(analyte, time) |>
  summarise(Q10 = quantile(conc, 0.1), Q50 = median(conc), Q90 = quantile(conc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, Q50, colour = analyte, fill = analyte)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Trough concentration (ng/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

## Exposure metric (equation 1) and PKNCA

The paper's primary exposure metric is the steady-state AUC of sunitinib plus
SU12662 for the initial 50 mg dose with cycle 1 apparent clearance,
AUCss = Dose / (CL / F) + Dose / (CL_SU12662 / F_SU12662) (equation 1). The model
reports the individual baseline clearances (`cl0`, `cl0_su12662`), `fdepot` and
`fm_su12662`, so the metric follows directly. PKNCA over the day-27 dosing
interval gives the corresponding simulated AUC0-24 and trough.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, treatment, Sunitinib = Cc, SU12662 = Cc_su12662, Total = Ctot) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Sunitinib, SU12662, Total), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
nca_dose <- events_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment) |>
  tidyr::crossing(analyte = c("Sunitinib", "SU12662", "Total"))
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + analyte + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + analyte + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 648, end = 672, auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
))
nca_df <- as.data.frame(nca_res)

# Equation 1 from each virtual patient's baseline parameters (mg*h/L = ug*h/mL).
eq1 <- sim_pk |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(
    id,
    Sunitinib = 50 * fdepot / cl0,
    SU12662 = 50 * fdepot * fm_su12662 / cl0_su12662,
    Total = Sunitinib + SU12662
  )
```

Supplementary Table S3 gives the medians of AUCss,DOSE50,CLcycle1 across the 165
patients of the exposure-response set (1.54, 0.67 and 2.19 ug*h/mL); Results give
the median combined steady-state trough, 81.8 ng/mL. The simulated AUC0-24 over
day 27 is in ng*h/mL, so the published values are multiplied by 1000.

```{r nca-compare}
reference_nca <- data.frame(
  analyte = c("Sunitinib", "SU12662", "Total"),
  auclast = 1000 * c(1.54, 0.67, 2.19),
  cmin = c(NA, NA, 81.8)
)
sim_nca <- nca_df |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmin")) |>
  select(analyte, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_nca,
  reference = reference_nca,
  by = "analyte",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmin = "ng/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median simulated day-27 AUC0-24 and trough versus the published medians of AUCss,DOSE50,CLcycle1 (Table S3) and Ctrough,ss (Results).")
```

```{r nca-check}
eq1_med <- eq1 |>
  summarise(across(c(Sunitinib, SU12662, Total), median))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Analyte = c("Sunitinib", "SU12662", "Total"),
    "Equation 1, median (ug*h/mL)" = unlist(eq1_med),
    "Table S3 median (ug*h/mL)" = c(1.54, 0.67, 2.19),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = 2, caption = "Equation 1 exposure from the virtual patients' baseline parameters."
)

# Equation 1 is a true steady state, which the day-27 interval is not: the
# SU12662 peripheral volume fills slowly (Vp/Q is about 380 h in a typical
# patient and far longer in some). The structural check therefore switches the
# time course off and doses daily for 200 days, after which the dosing-interval
# AUC must equal Dose * F / CL exactly. Two typical patients: the reference man
# and a 70-year-old, 60-kg woman with albumin 35 g/L, so the sex effects on F
# and fm and every covariate term are exercised.
typ_flat <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk) |>
  rxode2::ini(cl_time_hyp = 0, cl_time_hyp_su12662 = 0, v_time_hyp = 0, v_time_hyp_su12662 = 0)
ss_pat <- data.frame(id = 1:2, SEXF = c(0, 1), AGE = c(60, 70), WT = c(82.4, 60), ALB = c(41, 35))
ss_events <- bind_rows(
  expand.grid(id = 1:2, day = 0:199, cmt = c("depot", "depot_su12662"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    mutate(time = 24 * day, evid = 1L, amt = 50, dvid = NA_integer_) |>
    select(-day),
  expand.grid(id = 1:2, time = c(0, 199 * 24 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 23.99))) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  left_join(ss_pat, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
ss_sim <- solve_typical(typ_flat, events = ss_events, returnType = "data.frame")
ss_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(ss_sim |>
    filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    select(id, time, Sunitinib = Cc, SU12662 = Cc_su12662) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Sunitinib, SU12662), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc"),
  conc ~ time | analyte + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ss_events |> filter(evid == 1, cmt == "depot") |> select(id, time, amt) |>
    tidyr::crossing(analyte = c("Sunitinib", "SU12662")), amt ~ time | analyte + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 199 * 24, end = 200 * 24, auclast = TRUE)
))
ss_check <- as.data.frame(ss_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, analyte, auc = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(
    ss_sim |>
      filter(time == 0) |>
      transmute(id, Sunitinib = 1000 * 50 * fdepot / cl,
        SU12662 = 1000 * 50 * fdepot * fm_su12662 / cl_su12662) |>
      pivot_longer(c(Sunitinib, SU12662), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "expected"),
    by = c("id", "analyte")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc / expected - 1))
knitr::kable(ss_check, digits = 2,
  caption = "Steady-state dosing-interval AUC (ng*h/mL) with the time course switched off, against Dose * F / CL.")
# Same parameters on both sides: only trapezoidal error over a 13-point grid.
stopifnot(all(abs(ss_check$pct_diff) < 1))

# Against the published medians: a mis-transcribed clearance or a unit slip
# moves the whole distribution by tens of percent.
pub <- c(Sunitinib = 1.54, SU12662 = 0.67, Total = 2.19)
stopifnot(all(abs(100 * (unlist(eq1_med)[names(pub)] / pub - 1)) < 20))
```

The simulated medians sit close to the published ones. The virtual cohort draws its
covariates from the exposure-response set summary statistics, not from the
individual data, so an exact match is not expected.

## Time-varying clearance (Figure 2a)

```{r tv-cl, fig.cap = "Typical apparent clearance relative to its baseline value. Solid: the model, CL0 / (1 + beta * week) as printed in Supplementary S2. Dashed: the straight line 1 - beta * week. Replicates Figure 2a of Liu 2026."}
typ_pk <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk)
tgrid <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 24 * 7 * 24, by = 24), evid = 0L, amt = 0,
  cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, AGE = 60, WT = 82.4, ALB = 41, SEXF = 0)
typ_tv <- solve_typical(typ_pk, events = tgrid, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(week = time / 168, Sunitinib = cl / cl0, SU12662 = cl_su12662 / cl0_su12662)
typ_tv |>
  select(week, Sunitinib, SU12662) |>
  pivot_longer(-week, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "ratio") |>
  mutate(linear = 1 - ifelse(analyte == "Sunitinib", 0.00365, 0.00801) * week) |>
  ggplot(aes(week / (30.4375 / 7), ratio, colour = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = linear), linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.7, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (months)", y = "Fraction of initial CL/F", colour = NULL)

end_c4 <- typ_tv |> filter(week == 24)
decline <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Sunitinib CL/F", "SU12662 CL/F", "Sunitinib V/F", "SU12662 V/F"),
  Model = 100 * (1 - c(end_c4$cl / end_c4$cl0, end_c4$cl_su12662 / end_c4$cl0_su12662,
    end_c4$vc / end_c4$vc0, end_c4$vc_su12662 / end_c4$vc0_su12662)),
  "beta x 24 weeks" = 100 * 24 * c(0.00365, 0.00801, 0.00168, 0.0125),
  "Published decrease" = c(8.8, 19.2, 4.0, 30.0),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(decline, digits = 1,
  caption = "Percent decrease by the end of cycle 4 (24 weeks) in a typical patient.")
stopifnot(
  # The model equation, exactly.
  abs(end_c4$cl / end_c4$cl0 - 1 / (1 + 0.00365 * 24)) < 1e-6,
  abs(end_c4$cl_su12662 / end_c4$cl0_su12662 - 1 / (1 + 0.00801 * 24)) < 1e-6,
  # The published percentages are beta x 24 weeks.
  all(abs(decline[["beta x 24 weeks"]] - decline[["Published decrease"]]) < 0.1)
)
```

The published decreases (8.8%, 19.2%, 4.0%, 30.0%) equal beta x 24 weeks, the
first-order approximation of the printed hyperbolic form. The model follows the
printed equation, which gives 8.1%, 16.1%, 3.9% and 23.1%. See the assumptions
section.

## Covariate effects on exposure (Figure 3b)

```{r cov-exposure}
cov_grid <- data.frame(
  label = c("Reference", "Age 47 y", "Age 74 y", "Albumin 33 g/L", "Albumin 46 g/L",
    "Age +10 y", "Albumin +10%"),
  AGE = c(60, 47, 74, 60, 60, 70, 60),
  ALB = c(41, 41, 41, 33, 46, 41, 45.1),
  WT = 82.4, SEXF = 0
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
cov_typ <- solve_typical(typ_pk, events = cov_grid, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(label = cov_grid$label,
    auc_sun = 50 * fdepot / cl0, auc_su = 50 * fdepot * fm_su12662 / cl0_su12662)
ref <- cov_typ[1, ]
cov_tab <- cov_typ |>
  transmute(label, "Sunitinib CL/F ratio" = cl0 / ref$cl0,
    "SU12662 CL/F ratio" = cl0_su12662 / ref$cl0_su12662,
    "Sunitinib AUCss ratio" = auc_sun / ref$auc_sun,
    "SU12662 AUCss ratio" = auc_su / ref$auc_su)
knitr::kable(cov_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Typical-patient clearance and exposure relative to the model reference (age 60 years, albumin 41 g/L, 82.4 kg, man).")
# Results: a 10-year increase in age lowers CL/F by 5.7% (sunitinib) and 7.6%
# (SU12662); exactly exp(10 * theta_AGE).
stopifnot(
  abs(100 * (1 - cov_tab[["Sunitinib CL/F ratio"]][6]) - 5.7) < 0.05,
  abs(100 * (1 - cov_tab[["SU12662 CL/F ratio"]][6]) - 7.6) < 0.05
)
```

A 10% higher albumin lowers both clearances by 4.7%, the figure the Results quote
for the AUC increase (the AUC ratio itself is 1/0.953 = 1.049). For albumin the
Figure 3b point estimates (about 0.89 at 33 g/L and 1.03 at 46 g/L) agree with the
table above. The Figure 3b age panels show a wider spread (about 0.85 and 1.17 for
sunitinib at 47 and 74 years) than the Table S2 age coefficients imply (0.93 and
1.09); the model uses Table S2, which also reproduces the 5.7% and 7.6% per
decade that the Results state.

# Multistate model

The multistate model propagates the probabilities of the six states on a week
axis. All transitions except two have constant hazards. Stable disease -> response
is a decreasing Weibull hazard in time since the first dose. Progression -> death
is a log-logistic function of the subject's time to progression, supplied as the
covariate `T_PROGRESSION`: once a subject has progressed, that hazard is constant
and lower the later the progression happened. This is the form in which the
source fitted the model, with each subject's observed transition times in the
data. From baseline, though, the time to progression is not yet known. The
marginal probabilities of stable disease, response and the two discontinuation
states do not depend on it and come straight from the ODEs. Overall survival
integrates over the time-to-progression distribution, and below it is obtained by
simulating individual patient histories from the model's hazards.

```{r ms-setup}
mod_ms <- readModelDb("Liu_2026_sunitinib_multistate")
ref_cov <- data.frame(ALB = 41, HGB = 130, AGE = 57, ECOG_GE1 = 0, T_DIAG_CANCER = 200)
week_grid <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, seq(6, 156, by = 2))
# T_PROGRESSION = time: the k36 column then reads lambda36 for a progression at
# that time. It does not affect the stable, response or discontinuation states.
typ_ms <- solve_typical(mod_ms,
  events = data.frame(id = 1L, time = week_grid, evid = 0L, cmt = "s_stable") |>
    bind_cols(ref_cov) |>
    mutate(T_PROGRESSION = time),
  returnType = "data.frame")
```

## Closed-form and mass-balance checks

From stable disease the competing hazards are the Weibull stable -> response hazard
and four constants, so the probability of remaining in stable disease has the closed
form `exp(-(scale12 * t)^shape12 - (k13 + k14 + k15 + k16) * t)`. The ODE solution
must match it, and the six probabilities must sum to one.

```{r ms-closed-form}
c1 <- with(typ_ms[2, ], k13 + k14 + k15 + k16)
cf_stable <- exp(-(0.0471 * typ_ms$time)^0.844 - c1 * typ_ms$time)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(typ_ms$prob_stable_disease / cf_stable - 1)) < 1e-4,
  max(abs(typ_ms$prob_state_sum - 1)) < 1e-8
)
```

## Individual patient histories

Each history starts in stable disease. The time of leaving stable disease solves
`(scale12 * t)^shape12 + c1 * t = E` for a unit-exponential draw `E`; the
destination is drawn in proportion to the hazards at that time. Every later
sojourn is exponential, with the progression -> death hazard read from the model
at the drawn time to progression. All hazards come from the model's own output,
so the simulation exercises the shipped equations rather than a re-implementation
of them.

```{r ms-des-functions}
lookup_k36 <- function(k36_table, ids, ttp) {
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(ids))
  for (i in which(!is.na(ttp))) {
    tab <- k36_table[k36_table$id == ids[i], ]
    out[i] <- approx(tab$time, tab$k36, xout = min(ttp[i], max(tab$time)))$y
  }
  out
}

draw_dest <- function(h, states) {
  u <- runif(nrow(h)) * rowSums(h)
  states[1 + rowSums(u > t(apply(h, 1, cumsum)))]
}

simulate_histories <- function(hz, k36_table, nrep, fu = 156) {
  tr <- hz[rep(seq_len(nrow(hz)), each = nrep), ]
  c1 <- tr$k13 + tr$k14 + tr$k15 + tr$k16
  e1 <- rexp(nrow(tr))
  t1 <- vapply(seq_along(e1), function(i) {
    uniroot(function(t) (0.0471 * t)^0.844 + c1[i] * t - e1[i], c(0, 1e5), tol = 1e-10)$root
  }, numeric(1))
  h12 <- 0.0471 * 0.844 * (0.0471 * t1)^(0.844 - 1)
  dest1 <- draw_dest(cbind(h12, tr$k13, tr$k14, tr$k15, tr$k16), 2:6)
  t2 <- t1 + rexp(nrow(tr), tr$k23 + tr$k24 + tr$k25 + tr$k26)
  dest2 <- draw_dest(cbind(tr$k23, tr$k24, tr$k25, tr$k26), 3:6)
  ttp <- ifelse(dest1 == 3, t1, ifelse(dest1 == 2 & dest2 == 3, t2, NA))
  t_disc <- ifelse(dest1 %in% 4:5, t1, ifelse(dest1 == 2 & dest2 %in% 4:5, t2, NA))
  disc <- ifelse(dest1 %in% 4:5, dest1, ifelse(dest1 == 2 & dest2 %in% 4:5, dest2, NA))
  k36 <- lookup_k36(k36_table, tr$id, ttp)
  t_death <- ifelse(!is.na(ttp), ttp + rexp(nrow(tr), ifelse(is.na(k36), 1, k36)),
    ifelse(!is.na(t_disc), t_disc + rexp(nrow(tr), tr$k46),
      ifelse(dest1 == 6, t1, t2)))
  # Endpoint derivation as in Supplementary S3: TTP censored at death without
  # progression or at discontinuation; time to discontinuation due to AEs
  # censored at progression, discontinuation for other reasons or death.
  ttp_time <- pmin(ifelse(is.na(ttp), pmin(t_death, t_disc, na.rm = TRUE), ttp), fu)
  ae_time <- pmin(t_death, ttp, t_disc, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(
    id = tr$id, dest1 = dest1, dest2 = ifelse(dest1 == 2, dest2, NA),
    t1 = t1, t2 = ifelse(dest1 == 2, t2, NA), t_disc = t_disc, disc = disc, t_death = t_death,
    ttp_time = ttp_time, ttp_event = !is.na(ttp) & ttp <= fu,
    os_time = pmin(t_death, fu), os_event = t_death <= fu,
    ae_time = pmin(ae_time, fu), ae_event = disc %in% 4 & t_disc <= fu
  )
}

hazards_for <- function(cohort, grid = 0:160) {
  dd <- merge(cohort, data.frame(time = grid)) |>
    arrange(id, time) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "s_stable", T_PROGRESSION = time)
  out <- solve_typical(mod_ms, events = dd, returnType = "data.frame")
  # rxSolve omits the id column when only one subject is solved.
  if (!"id" %in% names(out)) out$id <- cohort$id[1]
  list(
    hz = out |> filter(time == 1) |> select(id, k13, k14, k15, k16, k23, k24, k25, k26, k46),
    k36 = out |> select(id, time, k36)
  )
}
```

First, a check of the simulator against the ODEs for the reference patient: the
fractions of 4000 simulated histories in stable disease, response and the two
discontinuation states must match the ODE probabilities within Monte Carlo error.
Those four states do not depend on the time to progression, so the ODEs give them
exactly.

```{r ms-des-check}
set.seed(20262)
ref_hz <- hazards_for(ref_cov |> mutate(id = 1L))
hist_ref <- simulate_histories(ref_hz$hz, ref_hz$k36, nrep = 4000, fu = 1e6)
check_weeks <- c(12, 26, 52)
# State occupancy at week w rebuilt from each history's transition times
# (fu = 1e6, so nothing is censored).
occ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(check_weeks, function(w) {
  h <- hist_ref
  in_disc <- !is.na(h$disc) & h$t_disc <= w & h$t_death > w
  data.frame(
    week = w,
    stable = mean(h$t1 > w),
    response = mean(h$dest1 == 2 & h$t1 <= w & h$t2 > w),
    disc_ae = mean(in_disc & h$disc == 4),
    disc_other = mean(in_disc & h$disc == 5)
  )
}))
ode <- typ_ms[match(check_weeks, typ_ms$time), ]
occ_cmp <- data.frame(
  week = rep(check_weeks, 4),
  state = rep(c("stable", "response", "disc_ae", "disc_other"), each = length(check_weeks)),
  simulated = c(occ$stable, occ$response, occ$disc_ae, occ$disc_other),
  ode = c(ode$prob_stable_disease, ode$prob_tumor_response, ode$prob_discontinuation_ae,
    ode$prob_discontinuation_other)
)
knitr::kable(occ_cmp, digits = 3,
  caption = "Reference patient: state occupancy in 4000 simulated histories versus the ODE probabilities.")
# Monte Carlo SE of a fraction from 4000 histories is at most 0.008.
stopifnot(all(abs(occ_cmp$simulated - occ_cmp$ode) < 0.03))
```

## Virtual cohort, transitions and survival (Figures 1, 2 and 4)

Two hundred virtual patients are drawn from the Supplementary Table S1 summary
statistics (truncated normal albumin, haemoglobin and age; 45% ECOG >= 1;
log-normal time since diagnosis with mean 38 and SD 53.6 months), each with 25
simulated histories over 36 months of follow-up.

```{r ms-cohort}
set.seed(20264)
n_ms <- 200
cohort_ms <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_ms),
  ALB = rtn(n_ms, 40.4, 4.8, 20, 49),
  HGB = rtn(n_ms, 124.3, 18.8, 86, 169),
  AGE = rtn(n_ms, 57.1, 10.3, 24, 87),
  ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(n_ms, 1, 0.45)
)
sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (53.6 / 38)^2))
cohort_ms$T_DIAG_CANCER <- 30.4375 *
  pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_ms, log(38) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog), 2.2), 339)

cohort_hz <- hazards_for(cohort_ms)
hist_cohort <- simulate_histories(cohort_hz$hz, cohort_hz$k36, nrep = 25)
```

```{r ms-transitions}
obs_counts <- c(Response = 85, Progression = 56, "Disc. AEs" = 15, "Disc. other" = 6, Death = 2)
sim_frac <- table(factor(hist_cohort$dest1, levels = 2:6)) / nrow(hist_cohort)
trans_tab <- data.frame(
  "From stable disease to" = names(obs_counts),
  "Observed (Figure 1)" = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", obs_counts, 100 * obs_counts / sum(obs_counts)),
  "Simulated" = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * as.numeric(sim_frac)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(trans_tab, caption = "First transition out of stable disease: Figure 1 counts (164 patients who left stable disease) versus the simulated cohort.")
resp_to_prog <- mean(hist_cohort$dest2[hist_cohort$dest1 == 2] == 3)
```

Of the simulated responders, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * resp_to_prog)` later
progressed, against 62 of the 71 observed responders with a further transition
(87%, Figure 1). The model sends more patients from stable disease to response
than were observed (see the assumptions section).

```{r ms-km, fig.cap = "Kaplan-Meier curves of simulated time to progression, overall survival and time to discontinuation due to adverse events (200 virtual patients x 25 histories). Compare with Figure 4 (VPC by study) and Figure 2d of Liu 2026."}
wk_per_month <- 30.4375 / 7
km_df <- function(time, event, endpoint) {
  fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1)
  data.frame(endpoint = endpoint, months = fit$time / wk_per_month, surv = fit$surv)
}
km_all <- bind_rows(
  km_df(hist_cohort$ttp_time, hist_cohort$ttp_event, "Time to progression"),
  km_df(hist_cohort$os_time, hist_cohort$os_event, "Overall survival"),
  km_df(hist_cohort$ae_time, hist_cohort$ae_event, "Time to disc. due to AEs")
)
ggplot(km_all, aes(months, surv)) +
  geom_step() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (months)", y = "Proportion without event")

km_median <- function(time, event) {
  unname(summary(survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1))$table["median"]) /
    wk_per_month
}
km_at <- function(time, event, months) {
  summary(survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1),
    times = months * wk_per_month, extend = TRUE)$surv
}
med_ttp <- km_median(hist_cohort$ttp_time, hist_cohort$ttp_event)
med_os <- km_median(hist_cohort$os_time, hist_cohort$os_event)
ae_36 <- km_at(hist_cohort$ae_time, hist_cohort$ae_event, 35.5)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Endpoint = c("Median TTP (months)", "Median OS (months)", "Free of disc. due to AEs at 36 months"),
  Simulated = c(med_ttp, med_os, ae_36),
  "Published (read from Figures 2d and 4)" = c("about 9-10", "about 20", "about 0.80-0.88"),
  check.names = FALSE
), digits = 2)
# Centre checks against values read from the published Kaplan-Meier curves:
# a wrong hazard unit (per day vs per week) or a sign error on a covariate
# effect moves these medians several-fold.
stopifnot(
  abs(med_ttp / 9.5 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(med_os / 20 - 1) < 0.25,
  ae_36 > 0.7, ae_36 < 0.95
)
```

## Confounder-fixed simulation (Figure 5)

Figure 5 of the paper sets every patient's albumin and age to the cohort medians
(41 g/L and 57 years) and keeps the other covariates. Because exposure is not in
the final model, low- and high-exposure groups have the same expected curves, which
is what the figure shows.

```{r ms-fig5, fig.cap = "Simulated time to progression and overall survival with albumin and age fixed at the cohort medians. Compare with Figure 5 of Liu 2026."}
set.seed(20265)
cohort_fix <- cohort_ms |> mutate(ALB = 41, AGE = 57)
fix_hz <- hazards_for(cohort_fix)
hist_fix <- simulate_histories(fix_hz$hz, fix_hz$k36, nrep = 25)
bind_rows(
  km_df(hist_fix$ttp_time, hist_fix$ttp_event, "Time to progression"),
  km_df(hist_fix$os_time, hist_fix$os_event, "Overall survival")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(months, surv)) +
  geom_step() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 31), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (months)", y = "Proportion without event")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Endpoint = c("Median TTP (months)", "Median OS (months)"),
  Simulated = c(km_median(hist_fix$ttp_time, hist_fix$ttp_event),
    km_median(hist_fix$os_time, hist_fix$os_event)),
  "Figure 5 (read from the curves)" = c("about 11", "about 18"),
  check.names = FALSE
), digits = 1)
```

Time to progression matches Figure 5. The simulated median overall survival is
longer than the roughly 18 months read from the figure; with albumin and age drawn
rather than fixed (previous section) it is about 19 months, close to the observed
curves of Figures 2d and 4.
The published simulation used the observed multistate dataset as its template,
with each patient's own haemoglobin, ECOG, time since diagnosis and follow-up,
whereas this cohort draws them independently from summary statistics.

## Exposure effects that were tested (Table 2)

For reference, the Table 2 hazard ratios per inter-quartile-range increase in
AUCss,DOSE50,CLcycle1 (1.37 ug*h/mL) convert to log-hazard slopes
`beta = log(HR) / 1.37` per ug*h/mL on `exp(beta * (AUC - 2.19))`. None is part of
the final model, and the baseline hazards of the models they were estimated in are
not published, so they are not shipped as model parameters.

```{r table2}
tab2 <- data.frame(
  Hazard = c("Stable -> progression", "Stable -> disc. AEs", "Progression -> death",
    "Stable -> progression (adj. age, albumin)", "Progression -> death (adj. albumin)",
    "Time to first dose reduction"),
  HR_IQR = c(0.71, 1.48, 0.78, 1.13, 0.94, 2.10)
) |>
  mutate(beta = log(HR_IQR) / 1.37)
knitr::kable(tab2 |> rename("HR per IQR" = HR_IQR, "beta (per ug*h/mL)" = beta), digits = 3)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Hyperbolic versus linear time course.** Supplementary S2 prints the time course
  twice as `CL/F = CL0/F / (1 + beta * T)` (and the same for Vc/F and Vp/F), and
  Table S2 footnote 6 repeats it. The main text calls the change a "linear decrease"
  and quotes decreases (8.8%, 19.2%, 4.0%, 30.0% by the end of cycle 4) that equal
  beta x 24 weeks, and Figure 2a draws straight lines ending near 0.91 and 0.81. The
  model follows the printed equation; the two readings differ by under 1 percentage
  point for sunitinib and 3 points for SU12662 CL/F over the 5-cycle span the data
  cover. Neither form is meant for extrapolation beyond about 30 weeks; with a
  negative individual beta the hyperbolic form grows without bound as `1 + beta * T`
  approaches zero.
* **Volume correlations.** Supplementary S2 says correlations were incorporated
  "between their respective Vc/F and Vp/F estimates", and Table S2 reports one
  "Correlation V/F (Parent-Met)" of 0.68. The maintainers apply 0.68 to both the
  parent-metabolite Vc/F pair and the Vp/F pair.
* **Two input depots.** The paper fixes separate absorption rate constants for the
  two compounds (Table S2) and states F_SU12662 = F_sunitinib x fm, i.e. SU12662
  appears through its own first-order input of a fraction of the sunitinib dose
  rather than through a formation clearance. Users dose the full sunitinib amount
  into both `depot` and `depot_su12662`. Amounts are on a mass basis; no
  molecular-weight conversion between sunitinib and SU12662 is applied, as in the
  paper's equation 1.
* **Time origin.** The time-varying terms use time since the first dose, in weeks;
  the first dose must be at `t = 0`.
* **Progression -> death hazard.** Table S4 names the time scale of this hazard
  "Time to Prog." and the text says it "decreased with longer time to progression".
  The log-logistic function itself is not printed. The maintainers use the same
  rate parameterisation the paper prints for its Weibull hazards,
  `scale * shape * (scale * TTP)^(shape - 1) / (1 + (scale * TTP)^shape)`, evaluated
  at the time to progression and held constant after progression.
* **Weibull stable -> response hazard.** With the printed parameterisation the
  virtual cohort leaves stable disease for response more often (about two thirds)
  than the 52% observed in Figure 1, and for progression less often (about 22% versus
  34%); median TTP and OS nonetheless match the published curves. The alternative
  `scale * t^shape` cumulative hazard brings the response share to about 54% but
  raises discontinuation due to AEs to about 15% (9% observed). The printed form is
  kept. The virtual cohort is built from summary statistics, which also contributes:
  the stable -> progression covariate effects are large (one SD of age alone changes
  the hazard 2.5-fold).
* **Background mortality.** Table S4 footnote d gives the Gompertz-Makeham natural
  death rate `0.0007 + 0.00018645 * exp(0.11425 * (age - 30))` per year. It is
  evaluated at baseline age and converted with 52.1429 weeks per year, as in the
  same group's Liu 2023 control stream. At age 57 it is about 9e-5 per week.
* **Time since diagnosis.** The paper's covariate is the dichotomy > 1 year versus
  <= 1 year. The model takes the canonical continuous `T_DIAG_CANCER` in days and
  applies the cut at 365.25 days.
* **Placeholder residual.** The source fits the multistate model with the exact
  likelihood of the observed transitions and has no residual error. A tiny additive
  error (`addSd = 0.001`) on `prob_death` lets nlmixr2 accept the model; it is not
  from the paper.
* **Time to first dose reduction.** The parametric time-to-event model for the first
  dose reduction (50 to 37.5 mg/day) is described only through its exposure hazard
  ratio (Table 2, 2.10 per IQR); its baseline hazard and distribution are not
  published, so it is not shipped.
* **Figure 3b age effect.** The Figure 3b age panels imply a larger age effect on
  exposure than the Table S2 coefficients; the model uses Table S2, which reproduces
  the per-decade clearance changes stated in the Results.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Covariates are drawn from the Supplementary Table S1 means,
  SDs and ranges, independently of each other; the paper's individual data and
  correlation structure (Supplementary Figure S1) are not available.
